images.title: Switching signs moves the total by an even amount
images.purpose: Shows that switching the signs of 7 and 9 in 2 + 7 + 4 + 9 + 6 changes the total from 28 to −4, a change of 2 × 16 = 32, so the parity stays even.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A before line above an after line, joined by one downward arrow with a short label.
images.exact_structure: Top line in large dark text: 2 + 7 + 4 + 9 + 6 = 28. Bottom line directly below: 2 − 7 + 4 − 9 + 6 = −4. In both lines the numbers 7 and 9 sit inside reddish purple (#CC79A7) outlined rounded boxes, so exactly 4 boxes in all; the switched signs in the bottom line are drawn reddish purple (#CC79A7). One thick grey (#6B7280) arrow points from the top line down to the bottom line on the right side, labelled changes by 2 × 16 = 32. Under the bottom line, one rounded green (#009E73) tag: both even. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Switching signs changes the total by twice the switched numbers, so the parity never changes.
images.description: Shows that switching the signs of 7 and 9 in 2 + 7 + 4 + 9 + 6 changes the total from 28 to −4, a change of 2 × 16 = 32, so the parity stays even.
images.teaching_notes: Same idea extends to any count of numbers.

image_decisions.why: A before and after pair shows the change is twice a number, which is why parity is kept.
